# Expanded guide walkthroughs

Release 0.18.0, profile 4.0.0. October 16, 2026.

Three fictional students completed the actual browser flow. Each chose the same Austin lifestyle: one adult, a one-bedroom apartment, used compact car, one dinner out weekly, modest travel and entertainment, hobbies, and steady savings. The resulting before-tax target is $65K–$85K. Their different career choices do not alter that target.

| Student | Three broad pathway cards | Explicit final choice | First paid stage in plan | Practical conclusion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medical interests | Science & environment; Health & helping; Technology & data | Family physician, after comparing PA and NP | About $70K, published Dell Med resident example | College + MD/DO + residency, about 11 years on this route. Budget is tight before loan payments. Practice pay comes later. |
| Visual creative interests | Design & creativity; Technology & data; Engineering & building | Graphic designer | About $46K, TWC starting-wage proxy | Only Design has clear interest support; the other cards are labelled related options. Bachelor’s typical, portfolio and internships important. Starting pay falls short of the chosen lifestyle. |
| Practical electrical interests | Trades; Transport & production; Engineering & building | Electrician | About $44K, one Austin ETA apprentice schedule | Four years/8,000 hours in this example, Texas licensing. Starting training pay falls short of the chosen lifestyle. College technical/business study can broaden options. |

Medicine task answers support physician, physician assistant, and nurse practitioner without claiming to differentiate them conclusively. Creative answers support graphic design most strongly, with interface design and public relations sharing several tasks. Electrical answers support electrician most strongly; plumbing shares enough clues for comparison. HVAC stays accessible in the wider list rather than being artificially added to make three.

The read-only walkthrough pages use the current matching model and the same plan-creation function as the live guide. Each has the actual original profile answers, the eight task selections, pathway reasons, the final preparation and financial context, and three useful next steps. They never replace the visiting student's saved draft.

Changes made during this review:

- Removed the unprocessed experience essay and existing-assessment detour from the required guide; retained earlier notes.
- Increased interest breadth from 30 to 60 activities, ten per RIASEC theme.
- Increased experience/confidence areas from eight to twelve, kept separate from ability measurement.
- Increased follow-ups from four to eight per family, across all 12 families.
- Required three independently answered questions before a profession joins the shortlist.
- Added related alternatives when only one broad field is supported; uncertain and partial evidence stays labelled.
- Calibrated multi-theme ordering and ensured organising-only interests still reach relevant fields.
- Made first paid residency/apprenticeship the salary on profession cards; clarified NP preparation and added direct lifestyle links.
- Added an education/credential sentence to final plans so a major name alone does not stand in for a preparation route.
- Scaled question headings, answer text and padding down while retaining 18px answer text and accessible touch targets.
- Replaced repeating-decimal meal counts with weekly frequency and concise rounded detail.
- Fixed the final-question loop when a revisiting student still has an earlier unanswered prompt.

Evidence: `validation/expanded-journey-browser-2026-10-16.json`. Complete browser exports were compared to scripted outputs for all three cases. The research and calibration memo distinguishes behavioral checks from the real-student psychometric pilot still needed; no predictive validity is claimed.
